lines.text: I heard a scream for help while falling with my headlights off.
It was a type of silent scream a trap lover makes to escape a pending marriage,
a concussion, a set of walls caving inward, seething and simmering,
and a solitude of crowds and smiles.
I received an emergency call while tossing and turning.
It was a type of silent call a man makes to the mirror after midnight.
To digest the truth, a windless insomnia and epiphany of a road winding down.
After a day of life dilated at the sun as long and as wise as possible, we won't make it.
I was six I recall when the ghost of a dead and loveless seven-year-old child appeared
and shared that my parents marriage wouldn't last.
It was a type of warm and heavy breeze in winter
where a child is left home alone.
With curtains pulled and blinds up as far and as wise as possible to see flashing lights
and the whispering screams of two souls on a road winding down.
And no tears and no fucks, no love to give, old to teach.

passage.line: and shared that my parents marriage wouldn't last.
passage.why_fulcrum: The ghost child's prophecy. After it, the parents arguing in the car is no longer a scene he watches but a sentence coming true, and the closing 'no love to give' reads as what he learned at six.

answer.title: Straight Talk
answer.said: That's what my parents told me.
answer.why: Echoes the telling: a young voice reporting what he was told about his parents. Here no parent told him; a ghost did, and the archive says the plain version back.

passage.gesture_detail: His right palm lays flat on the living-room window glass at shoulder height, fingers spread, and stays pressed there through the line and the archive's answer.
passage.surface: window: the living-room window, curtains pulled and blinds up, onto the street where the car stands with its lights flashing

plate.why: Parents arguing in the car: the scene book gives this window with curtains pulled and blinds up and the car beyond it, so the glass is there to open into.

passage.staging: Medium from inside the living room, POET in profile at the window, right of frame; his flat palm on the glass at center; car light sweeps the room from outside.
